page: Amazon Web Services r7g.16xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server powered by 64-bit ARM architecture. Built upon AWS Graviton3 processors using the ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 microarchitecture, the instance provides 64 dedicated physical cores running at 2.6 GHz. Because each physical core corresponds to a single vCPU without simultaneous multithreading, execution threads avoid resource contention at the hardware level. The processor provides 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, backed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The platform includes 512.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a high memory density of 8.0 GB per vCPU.

Hardware capabilities also include a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps and support for cryptographic hardware acceleration via ARM AES extensions. The r7g.16xlarge does not include onboard local storage or discrete graphics processing units, requiring attached network storage for persistent file systems. Performance benchmarks reflect the strength of its memory and multi-core subsystems. The system attained a PassMark memory score of 3153.01 and memory bandwidth benchmarks reached 253.34 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 116.96 GB/sec for writes. Multi-threaded throughput is demonstrated by a Geekbench multi-core score of 20513.0 and strong Redis processing measuring 101.19 million SET operations per second.

The primary tradeoff of the r7g.16xlarge is its reliance on ARM64 architecture, which lacks x86-specific vector extensions such as AVX-512 and requires compatible software packages. The absence of local NVMe storage also shifts all high-IOPS storage demands onto network interfaces. Nevertheless, the high memory-to-core density makes the instance cost-efficient for scale-out workloads requiring large memory footprints without overpaying for excess compute cores. It is suited for in-memory databases like Redis, relational database engines, real-time analytics, large caching tiers, and multi-threaded compilation workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services r7g.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Graviton3 processor family, utilizing the ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 architecture. It delivers 64 physical cores and 64 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading, ensuring consistent per-core execution. The server provides 512 GB of system memory at an 8 GB per core allocation, alongside 30 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth via the Nitro hypervisor. It contains no local disk storage and features zero GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached volumes for persistent data. In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates exceptional memory throughput and strong multi-core computational performance, posting 101.19 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and strong scores across database operations. The Graviton3 platform offers high hardware efficiency for memory-dense workloads, though it lacks x86-specific instruction sets like AVX-512. The configuration is primarily matched with in-memory caching platforms, distributed key-value stores, relational database management systems, and large-scale parallel software compilation pipelines.
